heuristics.eligibility: Eight finite probabilities in [0,1]; a candidate requires clear unique source or unreplayed onset support. Quiet frames do not provide identity support. Every unique or replay interval still requires eligible coverage. Any clear competing NEW/onset identity, competing runner or overlap vetoes identification regardless of duration. Multiple speaker/capture epochs cannot be merged.
heuristics.ambiguity_budget: Nonclear unique speech and a clear foreign PROVEN replay edge consume the SAME contiguous/total/relative budget. Replay cannot enlarge the denominator or supply the candidate. Substantial clear foreign replay exceeding that budget is mixed. Nonclear replay cannot vote for identity. Missing evidence and discontinuities remain unavailable, not acoustic ambiguity.
heuristics.rationale: Preserve existing probability thresholds while requiring representative clear support. 120 ms contiguous and 200 ms total bound an acoustic edge/hole rather than a whole utterance; 20% of unique clear support prevents long silence/context or a long speaker from laundering a short correction. These are explicit reversible starting heuristics, not measured acoustic optima.
counterexamples: 100 ms proven replay A plus two seconds clear new B is identified B; 300 ms foreign replay A is mixed.
The same 100 ms A interval supplied as NEW source or unreplayed onset vetoes B even though it fits the replay budget.
Any clear 10 ms competing new speaker vetoes a long majority speaker; complete streaming 50 ms No. between A spans remains an independent B source.
A 200 ms contiguous uncertainty hole fails the 120 ms bound. Two separated 110 ms holes fail the 200 ms total bound.
20 ms uncertainty versus 80 ms clear support fails the 20% ratio; no absolute minimum rejects an otherwise clear short utterance.
A missing 10 ms central evidence interval is unavailable rather than treated as a low-confidence acoustic hole.

A real competing voice that never reaches clear support and does not trigger competing/overlap probabilities may be tolerated within the acoustic ambiguity budget. This is an explicitly accepted misassignment risk, not a proved speaker-accuracy guarantee.
Estimated lexical timing that genuinely encloses clear A and B cannot be assigned to B by duration majority. Coherent gray is preferred for that unit when no supported lexical partition exists.
